text.p: Koor Industries Ltd announced on Monday that it will join Makhteshim Chemical Works and Agan Chemical Manufacturers under one new holding company.
Shareholders in the two chemical companies will be offered to exchange their shares for shares in the new holding company, M.A.G.M. Chemical Holdings, to be traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.
The decision was made by the board of directors of Makhteshim and Agan.
Makhteshim and Agan, two of the biggest producers of generic agro-chemicals in the world, would be delisted and would become fully owned M.A.G.M. companies.

Koor said it would create a new company within M.A.G.M. that would hold the shares of Makhteshim and Agan, which would concentrate solely on agro-chemical activities. The other activities will be run by M.A.G.M.

"The proposed programme is an important step that will allow us to attain the strategic aim of the growth of each one of the companies," the company said in a statement. The plan will not bring a change to the activities of Makhteshim and Agan, but will allow them to raise bigger sums of money for future growth, the company said.
Makhteshim is 64.7 percent held by Koor Industries. Agan is 47 percent owned by Makhteshim.
In 1995 sales of Agan were $209 million and the net profit was $23 million. Sales of Makhteshim in 1995 totalled $449 million and net profits totalled $37.1 million.
